title: Add initiative and epic tiers above the issue
description: Add the initiative -> epic -> issue hierarchy with an epic executable scenario. Repairs LB-23-PLANNING-EXECUTABLE-SCENARIO by re-shaping the slice to store and attest the scenario and enforcing it in the contract, and LB-23-PLANNING-HIERARCHY-SEMANTICS by naming the construction surface and fixing cardinality, orphan, empty-parent, and roll-up semantics.

behaviors.title: The hierarchy is constructed through a named surface with defined cardinality
behaviors.trigger: An operator or agent creates an initiative and an epic and links issues to that epic through the named CLI commands and MCP tools
behaviors.expected: An issue has at most one epic parent and an epic has at most one initiative parent; a second parent link for the same child replaces the first rather than creating a second edge; and an issue with no epic parent remains valid and standalone
behaviors.verify: Against a disposable database, create an initiative and epic through the named surface, link two issues, re-link one to a different epic, and read back exactly one parent per child plus one unparented standalone issue

behaviors.title: The epic stores an executable scenario and records its attestation
behaviors.trigger: An epic is created with an executable scenario and a wired or live attestation that the scenario ran is recorded against it
behaviors.expected: The scenario text is persisted on the epic and the attestation is retrievable and linked to that epic; an epic without a recorded attestation reports its scenario as unattested
behaviors.verify: Against a disposable database, create an epic with a scenario through the named surface, read back the unattested state, record a wired attestation, and read back the attested state linked to that epic

behaviors.title: The epic completion gate requires shipped children and an attested scenario
behaviors.trigger: The epic completion gate evaluates an epic
behaviors.expected: complete only when the epic has at least one child issue, every child is shipping-ready, and its executable scenario is attested; blocked otherwise with the exact blocking issue ids and an explicit missing-attestation indicator; empty when the epic has no child issues, and empty is never complete
behaviors.verify: Against a disposable database, evaluate an epic across four cases - no children, unshipped child, all children shipped but scenario unattested, and all shipped with scenario attested - asserting empty, blocked with ids, blocked with the missing-attestation indicator, and complete respectively

behaviors.title: The portfolio read model exposes the hierarchy with per-tier disposition
behaviors.trigger: The portfolio read model is requested through the named CLI command or MCP tool
behaviors.expected: It returns initiative -> epic -> issue with an explicit disposition on every tier. An issue carries exactly its existing shipping disposition (ship, ship_with_debt, or hold), reusing that vocabulary rather than a new one. An epic carries complete, blocked, or empty per the settled epic completion gate. An initiative carries the same three literals: empty when it has no child epics, complete when it has at least one child epic and every child epic is complete, and otherwise blocked with the ids of every child epic that is blocked or empty. An empty child epic therefore blocks its initiative, because empty is never complete. Epics with no children and issues with no epic parent are included and never omitted from the output.
behaviors.verify: Against a disposable database seeded with one initiative containing a complete epic, a blocked epic, and an empty epic, plus a shipped issue, a held issue, and an orphaned issue, read the portfolio through both the CLI and MCP surfaces and assert every node's exact disposition, including the initiative reading blocked with blocking ids naming both the blocked and the empty epic, each issue's disposition equalling its shipping disposition, and the orphaned issue present

planning.outcome: Loopbreaker models strategic and grouping tiers above the issue, with an epic whose executable scenario must be attested before the epic can read complete.
planning.appetite: One hierarchy slice with concrete typed tables, a scenario attestation, and a portfolio read model.
non_goals: Rordi's unified entities table and data-driven schemas
Nesting beyond initiative to epic to issue
Automatically executing the epic scenario; this slice stores it and records an attestation

work_units.title: Add initiatives and epics tables and the construction/linking surface
work_units.done_when: The named CLI commands and MCP tools create tiers and link children with at-most-one-parent cardinality

work_units.title: Store the epic executable scenario and its attestation
work_units.done_when: An epic persists a scenario and a wired or live attestation can be recorded and retrieved against it

work_units.title: Roll up child shipping readiness and the scenario attestation
work_units.done_when: The gate returns complete, blocked with ids and missing-attestation, or empty by the defined rules

work_units.title: Expose the hierarchy with per-tier disposition
work_units.done_when: The portfolio read model returns every node including empty epics and orphaned issues, with initiative, epic, and issue dispositions computed by the defined roll-up rules

proofs.method: Create, link, and re-link through the named surface against a disposable database; assert one parent per child and a surviving standalone issue.
Create an epic with a scenario, assert unattested, record a wired attestation, assert attested and linked.
Four-case matrix (no children, unshipped child, unattested scenario, fully satisfied) asserting empty, blocked-with-ids, blocked-with-missing-attestation, and complete.

Seeded hierarchy with a complete, a blocked, and an empty epic under one initiative plus shipped, held, and orphaned issues, read through both CLI and MCP, asserting each tier's exact disposition and the initiative's blocking epic ids.

planning.production_wiring: New initiatives and epics tables in db.ts migrate(), with epics.initiative_id and issues.epic_id nullable foreign keys enforcing at-most-one parent per child, plus epics.executable_scenario TEXT. Scenario attestation reuses the existing evidence model with an epic_id linkage so tier and verdict rules stay in one place. Construction surface: `loopbreaker initiative`, `loopbreaker epic`, and `loopbreaker portfolio` CLI commands in src/cli.ts emitting the standard TOON envelope, plus review_upsert_initiative, review_upsert_epic, review_attest_epic_scenario, and review_portfolio MCP tools in src/mcp.ts. Roll-up and the completion gate live in src/domain.ts beside the existing shipping derivation and reuse each child's shipping.ready. The single-issue substrate is unchanged.
planning.rollback: The tiers are additive and every parent edge is nullable. Drop the tier tables and the portfolio surface and issues evaluate exactly as they do today, standalone, with no data loss.
planning.migration: Additive tables and nullable parent columns; every existing issue starts with a null epic_id and is reported as an orphan by the portfolio read model rather than being hidden.

risks.risk: Hierarchy complicates the clean single-issue substrate.
risks.mitigation: The issue substrate is untouched; the portfolio is a separate read model.

risks.risk: Requiring a scenario attestation blocks epics whose children all shipped.
risks.mitigation: That is the intended semantics; the blocked disposition names the missing attestation explicitly so the gap is actionable.

risks.risk: Orphaned issues could be hidden by a hierarchy-first read model.
risks.mitigation: LB-23-B4 enforces that no issue is ever omitted from the portfolio output.
